messages:
maya: heads up — saw a quota spike this morning that looked like project A traffic being attributed to org-level keys. service routing fell back to cheapest model and our SLA alerts fired. anyone else see weird key->project attribution?
ria: saw that too, :eyes:. on traces it looks like some requests come in with `x-origin: project` but we resolve to org key because of our key-affinity fallback.
sam: can you paste the raw header dump? are these ephemeral tokens or long-lived keys?
maya: pasted a scrubbed example below:
```
Authorization: Bearer sa_abc123
x-org-id: org-42
x-project-id: proj-alpha
```
The token looks like an org SA, but the request included x-project-id from the client. The auth resolver currently prefers token claims over explicit header, so it attributes to org.
jordan: hmm that is expected behavior right now (token wins). The problem is our routing policy then collapses quota to org bucket which is much lower per-token cap for that customer leading to fallback to cheaper models.
ria: UX ask — can the console show both "authenticated identity" and "effective attribution"? teams keep asking why their project-level quota didn't match billing.
sam: +1 on console visibility. Also we should add telemetry flag for "auth-decision-reason" (e.g. token_claims > header_override > proxy_hint). Would make triage easier.
maya: agree. For short-term mitigation: proposal to prefer explicit `x-project-id` when token is org-scoped and `x-project-id` matches a valid project under that org. Only enable via feature flag for 48h canary. thoughts?
jordan: I worry about impersonation risk. If a client spoofs `x-project-id` but token is org-level, they could route to a different project quota. Need an authorization check: verify token has delegation/impersonation claim for the project.
ria: yeah we need a guard: allow header override only when token has `delegated_projects` claim or when request originates from trusted subnet (internal). Also surface a warning in console when override used.
sam: implementation note: change resolver order in auth-service -> attribution layer: currently `claims -> header` becomes `claims -> header if delegated -> header deny`. Minimal change: add `header_validated` boolean.
maya: rollout plan: create feature flag `auth.header_override_enabled`. Start with off, enable for 5% of orgs (canary), monitor telemetry metric `attribution.override.accepted` and `attribution.override.rejected`. If accept rate spikes or billing mismatches, roll back.
jordan: add dashboards: per-org breakdown showing % of requests where token attribution != effective attribution, and top reasons (missing delegation claim, routing fallback). Also add an alert if followed-by model fallback rate > 1% after override accepted.
deploy-bot: canary deploy queued: auth-service v3.12.0 -> canary cluster. Change set: attribution header validation + feature flag. Link: https://ci.internal/redwood/builds/12345 :rocket:
maya: Thanks. I'll draft console change with a small badge that reads "Attribution: token(org) -> project(proj-alpha) (override)" and a hover tooltip showing reason and trace id.
ria: pinging product to confirm wording and whether we need a billing-side migration note.
sam: quick checklist for the PR:
- [ ] add `header_validated` check in attribution
- [ ] emit telemetry tags: `auth.attribution.reason`, `auth.override`
- [ ] console badge + telemetry drilldown
- [ ] rollout flag + canary config
- [ ] unit/e2e tests for spoof header scenarios
jordan: also add an InfoSec signoff step for the canary since this touches auth decisioning.
maya: agreed. I'll open the RFC and include the telemetry dashboards mock. File issues for release pipeline.
ria: cool — will follow up with product & billing. Thanks all.
